Guidance-vs-law gap: the Legislative Council Staff 'Colorado Law Summary: CORA' (rev. 9/18/2024) describes a deposit for requests exceeding one hour of research and retrieval and a true-up (additional payment / partial refund) that appears nowhere in the statute; the AG's Formal Opinion No. 01-1 (2001) predates the 2007/2014/2023 fee amendments (its $1.25/page figure is superseded). Colorado has no administrative-code CORA fee schedule and no state 'uniform fee schedule' binding local bodies; CORA's fee section applies uniformly to the state, agencies, institutions and political subdivisions (cities and towns), with carve-outs only for the secretary of state and department of personnel and a separate CCJRA regime (§ 24-72-306) for criminal-justice records where the municipal governing body sets fee amounts.

After the first hour of time has been expended, the custodian may charge a fee for the research and retrieval of public records that shall not exceed thirty dollars per hour. || On July 1, 2019, and by July 1 of every five-year period thereafter, the director of research of the legislative council appointed pursuant to section 2-3-304 (1) shall adjust the maximum hourly fee specified in subsection (6)(a) of this section in accordance with the percentage change over the period in the United States department of labor, bureau of labor statistics, consumer price index for Denver-Aurora-Lakewood for all items and all urban consumers, or its successor index. The director of research shall post the adjusted maximum hourly fee on the website of the general assembly. || Section 24-72-205 (6) (b), C.R.S., requires the Director of Research of the Legislative Council Staff to adjust the Colorado Open Records Act maximum hourly fee for the research and retrieval of public documents for inflation on July 1, 2019, and each five years thereafter. The maximum hourly fee increased from $30.00 to $33.58 on July 1, 2019. Effective July 1, 2024, the maximum hourly fee will increase to $41.37. Before increasing the fee, government entities must revise and publish their Colorado Open Records Act policies to include the new fee.

resolutions.source_language: Upon request for records transmission by a person seeking a copy of any public record, the custodian shall transmit a copy of the record by United States mail, other delivery service, facsimile, or electronic mail. No transmission fees may be charged to the record requester for transmitting public records via electronic mail. Within the period specified in section 24-72-203 (3)(a), the custodian shall notify the record requester that a copy of the record is available but will only be sent to the requester once the custodian either receives payment or makes arrangements for receiving payment for all costs associated with records transmission and for all other fees lawfully allowed, unless recovery of all or any portion of such costs or fees has been waived by the custodian. Upon either receiving such payment or making arrangements to receive such payment at a later date, the custodian shall send the record to the requester as soon as practicable but no more than three business days after receipt of, or making arrangements to receive, such payment.

Binds every CORA custodian (state, agencies, institutions, political subdivisions incl. cities/towns). Ceiling; the municipality sets its own rate at or below $41.37 in its published policy. Memo phrase 'first hour of time expended on each request' supports a per-request reading of the free hour.

new_rules.legal_concept: No per-page fee for records provided in digital or electronic format
new_rules.atomic_rule: A custodian shall not charge a per-page fee for providing records in a digital or electronic format.
new_rules.trigger: Records are provided in a digital or electronic format
new_rules.source_language: A custodian may charge a fee not to exceed twenty-five cents per standard page for a copy of a public record or a fee not to exceed the actual cost of providing a copy, printout, or photograph of a public record in a format other than a standard page; except that a custodian shall not charge a per-page fee for providing records in a digital or electronic format.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)
new_rules.notes: Added by SB 23-286 (2023). Fixed $0 per page for digital/electronic delivery; the 25¢ ceiling (CO-0016) applies only to paper standard-page copies. Actual-cost charges for the medium/format (CO-0017) and research-and-retrieval fees remain available.

new_rules.legal_concept: Copy transmitted only after payment or payment arrangements; availability notice; three-business-day send
new_rules.atomic_rule: When a requester asks for transmission of a copy, the custodian shall, within the § 24-72-203(3)(a) period, notify the requester that a copy is available but will be sent only once the custodian receives payment or makes arrangements for payment of all transmission costs and all other fees lawfully allowed (unless waived by the custodian), and shall then send the record as soon as practicable but no more than three business days after receiving payment or making payment arrangements.
new_rules.trigger: Requester seeks transmission (mail, delivery service, fax, or e-mail) of a copy of a public record
new_rules.clock_spec: notice within the 24-72-203(3)(a) period (3 working days, extendable) from request; record sent ≤ 3 business-days from receipt of payment or from making arrangements to receive payment
new_rules.source_language: Upon request for records transmission by a person seeking a copy of any public record, the custodian shall transmit a copy of the record by United States mail, other delivery service, facsimile, or electronic mail. No transmission fees may be charged to the record requester for transmitting public records via electronic mail. Within the period specified in section 24-72-203 (3)(a), the custodian shall notify the record requester that a copy of the record is available but will only be sent to the requester once the custodian either receives payment or makes arrangements for receiving payment for all costs associated with records transmission and for all other fees lawfully allowed, unless recovery of all or any portion of such costs or fees has been waived by the custodian. Upon either receiving such payment or making arrangements to receive such payment at a later date, the custodian shall send the record to the requester as soon as practicable but no more than three business days after receipt of, or making arrangements to receive, such payment.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)
new_rules.notes: Production gate: pay (or arrange payment) before release. Also functions as the statutory cost notice — no dollar/hour threshold; applies to every transmission request. Statute does not say what happens if the requester never pays (no withdrawal period). Mail/delivery-service transmission costs are chargeable; e-mail transmission is free (CO-0021).

new_rules.legal_concept: Credit card / electronic payment must be accepted if accepted for other services; processor fee pass-through
new_rules.atomic_rule: If a custodian allows the public to pay for any other service or product with a credit card or electronic payment, the custodian must allow the requester to pay any fee or deposit associated with the request by credit card or electronic payment, and may require the requester to pay any service charge or fee imposed by the payment processor.
new_rules.trigger: Custodian accepts credit-card or electronic payment for any other service or product
new_rules.source_language: If a custodian of a public record requested pursuant to this part 2 allows members of the public to pay for any other service or product provided by the custodian with a credit card or electronic payment, the custodian must allow the requester of the public record to pay any fee or deposit associated with the request with a credit card or via an electronic payment. The custodian may require a requester to pay any service charge or fee imposed by the processor of a credit card or electronic payment.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)
new_rules.notes: Added by SB 23-286 (2023). Conditional requirement (not unconditional). Statute recognizes a 'deposit associated with the request' but sets no deposit threshold or cap anywhere in CORA.

new_rules.legal_concept: Data-manipulation (programming) fee capped at actual cost
new_rules.atomic_rule: If, in response to a specific request, a political subdivision performs a manipulation of data to generate a record in a form it does not use, it may charge a reasonable fee not to exceed the actual cost of manipulating the data and generating the record.
new_rules.trigger: Custodian performs a manipulation of data to generate a record in a form not used by the public body
new_rules.source_language: If, in response to a specific request, the state or any of its agencies, institutions, or political subdivisions has performed a manipulation of data so as to generate a record in a form not used by the state or by said agency, institution, or political subdivision, a reasonable fee may be charged to the person making the request. Such fee shall not exceed the actual cost of manipulating the said data and generating the said record in accordance with the request. Persons making subsequent requests for the same or similar records may be charged a fee not in excess of the original fee.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)
new_rules.notes: Soft standard ('reasonable') bounded by 'actual cost of manipulating the said data and generating the said record'. No hourly figure. Applies expressly to political subdivisions.

new_rules.legal_concept: Subsequent requests for the same/similar manipulated-data record capped at the original fee
new_rules.atomic_rule: Persons making subsequent requests for the same or similar manipulated-data records may be charged a fee not in excess of the original fee.
new_rules.trigger: A later request for the same or similar record previously generated by data manipulation
new_rules.source_language: If, in response to a specific request, the state or any of its agencies, institutions, or political subdivisions has performed a manipulation of data so as to generate a record in a form not used by the state or by said agency, institution, or political subdivision, a reasonable fee may be charged to the person making the request. Such fee shall not exceed the actual cost of manipulating the said data and generating the said record in accordance with the request. Persons making subsequent requests for the same or similar records may be charged a fee not in excess of the original fee.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)
new_rules.notes: Scope limited to records generated by data manipulation under § 24-72-205(3); CORA has no general repeat-request or aggregation rule (aggregation of requests within 14 days was proposed in SB25-077 (vetoed 2025) and SB26-107 (postponed indefinitely 2026) and is not law).

new_rules.legal_concept: Fee basis for computer output other than word processing
new_rules.atomic_rule: If the public record is a result of computer output other than word processing, the fee for a copy, printout, or photograph may be based on recovery of the actual incremental costs of providing the electronic services and products together with a reasonable portion of the costs associated with building and maintaining the information system.
new_rules.trigger: Record is computer output other than word processing
new_rules.source_language: If the public record is a result of computer output other than word processing, the fee for a copy, printout, or photograph thereof may be based on recovery of the actual incremental costs of providing the electronic services and products together with a reasonable portion of the costs associated with building and maintaining the information system. Such fee may be reduced or waived by the custodian if the electronic services and products are to be used for a public purpose, including public agency program support, nonprofit activities, journalism, and academic research. Fee reductions and waivers shall be uniformly applied among persons who are similarly situated.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)
new_rules.notes: Soft standard: 'actual incremental costs' plus 'a reasonable portion' of system costs. No number. Interaction with the SB 23-286 prohibition on per-page fees for digital format (CO-9002) is not addressed in statute.

new_rules.legal_concept: Discretionary reduction/waiver of computer-output fee for public purposes; must be uniformly applied
new_rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may reduce or waive the computer-output fee if the electronic services and products are to be used for a public purpose, including public agency program support, nonprofit activities, journalism, and academic research; reductions and waivers shall be uniformly applied among similarly situated persons.
new_rules.trigger: Requester will use computer-output electronic services/products for a public purpose
new_rules.source_language: If the public record is a result of computer output other than word processing, the fee for a copy, printout, or photograph thereof may be based on recovery of the actual incremental costs of providing the electronic services and products together with a reasonable portion of the costs associated with building and maintaining the information system. Such fee may be reduced or waived by the custodian if the electronic services and products are to be used for a public purpose, including public agency program support, nonprofit activities, journalism, and academic research. Fee reductions and waivers shall be uniformly applied among persons who are similarly situated.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)
new_rules.notes: Discretionary ('may'), limited to § 24-72-205(4) computer-output fees. Uniformity duty is mandatory once a waiver policy is applied. No written-denial, purpose-statement or appeal procedure is prescribed.

new_rules.legal_concept: Specifically-prescribed fees (incl. certified copies) override the CORA copy fee
new_rules.atomic_rule: Where the fee for a certified copy or other copy, printout, or photograph of a record is specifically prescribed by law, the specific fee applies instead of the § 24-72-205(5) fee.
new_rules.trigger: A statute or other law specifically prescribes a fee for the certified copy or other copy requested
new_rules.source_language: In all cases in which a person has the right to inspect a public record, the person may request a copy, printout, or photograph of the record. The custodian shall furnish a copy, printout, or photograph and may charge a fee determined in accordance with subsection (5) of this section; except that, when the custodian is the secretary of state, fees shall be determined and collected pursuant to section 24-21-104 (3), and when the custodian is the executive director of the department of personnel, fees shall be determined and collected pursuant to section 24-80-102 (10). Where the fee for a certified copy or other copy, printout, or photograph of a record is specifically prescribed by law, the specific fee shall apply.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)
new_rules.notes: CORA itself sets no certification/certified-copy fee. Same subsection routes the secretary of state (§ 24-21-104(3)) and the department of personnel (§ 24-80-102(10)) to their own fee statutes — state-agency regime, not municipal. No municipal certified-copy fee statute was found in C.R.S. Title 31 (2026 ed.).

new_rules.legal_concept: Certified copies free of charge for U.S. veterans'-benefits eligibility
new_rules.atomic_rule: Whenever a copy of a public record is required by the U.S. veterans administration or another federal agency to determine a veteran's or dependent's eligibility for federal service-connected benefits, the official charged with custody of the record shall provide a certified copy without charge to the applicant, a person acting on the applicant's behalf, or the agency representative.
new_rules.trigger: Certified copy required by a federal agency for veterans'-benefits eligibility determination
new_rules.source_language: Whenever a copy of any public record is required by the United States veterans administration or its successors or any other agency of the government of the United States to be used in determining the eligibility of any person who has served in the armed forces of the United States or any dependent of such person to participate in benefits for such person made available by the laws of the United States in relation to such service in the armed forces of the United States, the official charged with the custody of such public records, without charge, shall provide the applicant for such benefits or any person acting on his behalf, or the representative of such bureau or other agency, with a certified copy of such record.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)
new_rules.notes: Mandatory waiver (fixed $0) for one narrow ground; applies to any 'official charged with the custody of such public records' (municipal custodians included). Cited by Colo. AG Formal Opinion No. 01-1 (July 5, 2001), Q10.

new_rules.legal_concept: Custodian may waive recovery of transmission costs and other fees
new_rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may waive recovery of all or any portion of the transmission costs and other lawfully allowed fees otherwise payable before a copy is sent.
new_rules.trigger: Custodian elects not to recover costs/fees on a transmission request
new_rules.source_language: Upon request for records transmission by a person seeking a copy of any public record, the custodian shall transmit a copy of the record by United States mail, other delivery service, facsimile, or electronic mail. No transmission fees may be charged to the record requester for transmitting public records via electronic mail. Within the period specified in section 24-72-203 (3)(a), the custodian shall notify the record requester that a copy of the record is available but will only be sent to the requester once the custodian either receives payment or makes arrangements for receiving payment for all costs associated with records transmission and for all other fees lawfully allowed, unless recovery of all or any portion of such costs or fees has been waived by the custodian. Upon either receiving such payment or making arrangements to receive such payment at a later date, the custodian shall send the record to the requester as soon as practicable but no more than three business days after receipt of, or making arrangements to receive, such payment.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)
new_rules.notes: General discretionary waiver recognized by the clause 'unless recovery of all or any portion of such costs or fees has been waived by the custodian'. No grounds, purpose statement, written denial, or appeal prescribed. Criminal-justice-record fees: § 24-72-306(1) 'may waive fees at their discretion' (CO-9013).

new_rules.legal_concept: Supervision-of-copying fee equals the copy fee; requester pays cost of outside copying facilities
new_rules.atomic_rule: When the requester makes the copy under the custodian's supervision, the custodian may charge the same fee for supervising the copying as it may charge for furnishing a copy under § 24-72-205(5), and if other facilities are necessary the requester pays the cost of providing them.
new_rules.trigger: Custodian lacks copying facilities and the requester makes the copy under supervision, or copying must occur at other facilities
new_rules.source_language: If other facilities are necessary, the cost of providing them shall be paid by the person desiring a copy, printout, or photograph of the record. The custodian may establish a reasonable schedule of times for making a copy, printout, or photograph and may charge the same fee for the services rendered in supervising the copying, printing out, or photographing as the custodian may charge for furnishing a copy, printout, or photograph under subsection (5) of this section.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)
new_rules.notes: Supervision fee is capped by reference to the (5)(a) copy-fee ceiling (25¢/standard page or actual cost for other formats).

new_rules.legal_concept: Criminal-justice-record fees: actual costs incl. personnel for search, retrieval, redaction; 25¢/page; municipal governing body sets amounts
new_rules.atomic_rule: For criminal justice records requested under CCJRA, a criminal justice agency (including a municipal police department) may assess reasonable fees not to exceed actual costs, including personnel and equipment, for search, retrieval, and redaction; may waive fees at its discretion; may charge not more than 25¢ per standard page or actual cost for other formats; and where the agency is a department of a municipality, the amount of such fees shall be established by the municipal governing body in accordance with this subsection.
new_rules.trigger: Request is for criminal justice records under C.R.S. 24-72-301 et seq. (CCJRA)
new_rules.source_language: Criminal justice agencies may assess reasonable fees, not to exceed actual costs, including but not limited to personnel and equipment, for the search, retrieval, and redaction of criminal justice records requested pursuant to this part 3 and may waive fees at their discretion. In addition, criminal justice agencies may charge a fee not to exceed twenty-five cents per standard page for a copy of a criminal justice record or a fee not to exceed the actual cost of providing a copy, printout, or photograph of a criminal justice record in a format other than a standard page. Where fees for certified copies or other copies, printouts, or photographs of criminal justice records are specifically prescribed by law, such specific fees shall apply. Where the criminal justice agency is an agency or department of any county or municipality, the amount of such fees shall be established by the governing body of the county or municipality in accordance with this subsection (1).
new_rules.effective_status: Current (C.R.S. 2026 edition, current through the 2026 Regular Session; § 24-72-205 last amended by SB 23-286, eff. Aug. 7, 2023)
new_rules.notes: Separate fee regime for municipal police/criminal-justice records: no free first hour, no $41.37 cap, redaction time expressly chargeable, and the fee amounts are expressly delegated to the municipal governing body (defers_to_city). Not amended 2024–2026 (source note: L. 2008 last).

new_rules.legal_concept: Legislative Council Staff guidance: deposit for requests exceeding one hour of research and retrieval; true-up
new_rules.atomic_rule: Per Legislative Council Staff guidance, before completing a request that will take more than one hour of research and retrieval time the custodian may require a deposit equal to the estimated staff time, and may require additional payment or make a partial refund if actual time differs from the estimate.
new_rules.trigger: Request expected to exceed one hour of research and retrieval time
new_rules.source_language: Before completing a request that will take more than one hour of research and retrieval time, the custodian may require the requestor to pay a deposit equal to the estimated staff time needed to comply with the request. If the actual time spent turns out to be more or less than the initial estimate, the custodian may require an additional payment or make a partial refund of the deposit, respectively.
new_rules.source_authority: Legislative Council Staff, 'Colorado Law Summary: Colorado Open Records Act (CORA)' (last reviewed 09/18/2024), p. 2–3
new_rules.notes: GUIDANCE, NOT LAW: CORA's text contains no deposit threshold, deposit cap, or true-up rule; the statute only recognizes that a 'deposit associated with the request' may exist (§ 24-72-205(7)) and requires the research-and-retrieval policy to state its 'applicable conditions' (§ 24-72-205(6)(a)). This row records the Legislative Council's description of practice; it does not bind municipalities. Manual verification recommended before treating the one-hour trigger or 'equal to estimated staff time' as a value.

applicability_notes: CORA § 24-72-205 binds every 'custodian' — state, agencies, institutions and political subdivisions; § 24-72-202(5) defines 'political subdivision' to include every city and town. All figures resolved here therefore apply to municipalities unless noted.

State-agency-only carve-outs: § 24-72-205(1)(a) routes secretary-of-state fees to § 24-21-104(3) and department-of-personnel fees to § 24-80-102(10); § 24-72-205(5)(b) 'reasonable fee for a certified transcript' applies only to institutions of higher education. None bind cities.

Municipal police / criminal-justice records are governed by CCJRA § 24-72-306(1), not CORA § 24-72-205: reasonable fees not to exceed actual costs incl. personnel and equipment for search, retrieval AND redaction; no free first hour; no $41.37 cap; discretionary waiver; and the fee amounts 'shall be established by the governing body of the ... municipality' — an express defers_to_city.

The $41.37 maximum is a CEILING and is chargeable only after the first hour and only under a written policy posted/published before the request is received; the Legislative Council also states entities must revise and publish their policies before increasing to the new figure.

Deposit items: statute recognizes deposits (§ 205(7)) but sets no threshold/cap; the one-hour deposit trigger and 'equal to estimated staff time' come only from Legislative Council Staff guidance (CO-9014) and do not bind municipalities.
Home-rule municipalities: CORA's applicability to home-rule cities was not separately researched in this pass; treat as all_public_bodies pending any municipal-association/case-law pass.
material_negatives: No graduated page bands, free-page allowance, overhead/fringe %, billing increment, or per-requestor periodic free hours in Colorado law.
No itemized-estimate threshold, requester response window, revision-notice %, or estimate validity period.
No statutory deposit threshold, deposit cap %, nonpayment withdrawal period, or overrun re-issue rule (Legislative Council guidance describes deposit practice; not law).
No request-level maximum fee, de-minimis threshold, or minimum fee.
No certified-copy fee number in CORA for municipalities; no municipal certification fee statute found in Title 31.
No per-recording / per-minute / free-minutes audio-video figures.
No commercial-purpose fee schedule or surcharge; no fee forfeiture for late response; no general repeat-request/aggregation rule (only the § 205(3) manipulated-data carry-forward cap).
No 2024–2026 enactment amended § 24-72-205; the two reform bills that would have (SB25-077 vetoed; SB26-107 postponed indefinitely) are not law.
